measurement.frame_bounds: a file encode emits Frame_Content_Size (flag 2) with Single_Segment_flag = 1, so the window equals the content size; a streaming (stdin) encode of the same bytes emits neither, leaving Window_Size up to (1<<41)+7*(1<<38) bytes per doc/zstd_compression_format.md -- a reader cannot enforce the contract's decoded-length limit before decompression unless the section profile forbids that form
measurement.determinism: level 3 output is byte-identical across runs and with -T4, but level 1 differs from level 3: encoder output is not canonical, so the contract's decoded-content identity is the branch that applies and only a decoder is a trust surface

REFERENCE_ONLY: frame format, entropy coders (FSE/Huffman), dictionaries, seekable format, the CLI and library
decision.contract_change: ATLAS-BINARY-WIRE-FORMAT.md Compression: a ZSTD section is one single-segment frame whose Frame_Content_Size equals decoded_length, with no Dictionary_ID and no skippable or trailing frame; Content_Checksum optional (decoded_content_hash authenticates); encoder output non-canonical, identity over decoded content
decision.not_absorbed_because: no consumer needs fewer bytes; a native codec would be thousands of lines serving nothing, and an external one a runtime dependency serving nothing

reopen_trigger: a published container (sealing / FAT mode, exit criterion E) whose size is a measured cost; then the smallest native unit is a decoder bounded by the pinned profile, since the encoder need not be canonical
